findings.title: Search order controls discovery
findings.claim: The focus finding is made to appear as the result of an ordered search: a chosen first point, a sequence of containers, and a final extraction make the located person the endpoint of procedure rather than an unshaped accident.
findings.mechanism: The context sequence in 12:76 supplies beginning, precedence, bounded containers, and extraction, while the focus passive finding supplies the legal endpoint. The trusted channel record names that sequence as the mechanism by which the hidden object becomes socially effective.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see how the passive discovery acquires procedural shape and why the final location carries the force of proof.
findings.containment: This adds a staged-search relation to the stated finding of the person in his pack. It does not deny the surface legal rule, assert an unstated motive for every search step, or turn the channel nomination into a claim that the ayah explicitly explains its own construction.

epistemic.reason: A trusted channel record supplies the ordered-search relation, and the packet supplies matching context occurrences, a focus carrier, and a concrete return to the focus finding.

findings.title: Jurisdictional bridge
findings.claim: The stated custom is the hinge that transfers custody across incompatible normative orders.
findings.mechanism: The following ayah says that taking the brother was unavailable under the king's dīn except through the disclosed device. The brothers' person-as-recompense formula therefore supplies the alternative norm that makes custody available.
